topics.topic: Declaration, ownership, and import source of BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS
questions: Which module declares and owns `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS`, now that State 3 no longer identifies the minute look's 60 seconds as a `data_provider` constant?

From which module does `module:instance_lifecycle` import `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS`, now that the changed State 3 passage assigns application of both 60-second schedules to `instance_lifecycle` and does not name either as a `data_provider` constant?
Is the backup look's 60-second interval owned directly by `module:instance_lifecycle`, or is it a `data_provider` constant named `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` that `instance_lifecycle` imports?

quotes:
The typed constants of the data closure, the one home of each value the
generated code reads that is not a setting of the environment (SPEC_STANDARD
§6.10, §15.3.1; reopened 2026-11-11, replacing the former
release_declarations module): the
artifact types with their owner services, the first release's one row
(`estimate`, PresuPro) (A22); A09 rule 2's table of the services, their
operations and their highest classes; the store version and the store's
temporary-name suffix (A17 rule 5); the kept and temporary backup prefixes,
neither beginning with the other, the daily time, the minute look and the
retention of 30 × 24 hours (A18 rules 1, 4, 5); the import file's size limit
(A19 rule 4); the release's own version and its contract version, which
every audit entry names (M09) and a backup's record names (A18 rule 1); the
address each surface listens on, which the configuration does not name
(A17 rules 1, 2); the owner session's limits — 8 hours, 30 minutes, the 15
minutes and five refusals of the sign-in, the 10 minutes of a confirmation,
the 60 seconds of the pass (A13); the request id's 128 characters (A01 rule
1), the alias's 40 (A02 rule 4), the 32 bytes of a secret value and of a
configured secret (A13 rule 7, A17 rule 3). The list names groups; the data
closure names each constant, and every one is exported.
judgement.why: State 3 assigns the minute-look constant to data_provider, names BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS among its exported constants, and State 4 says instance_lifecycle imports and applies it.

topics.topic: Caller responsible for the 60-second expired owner-session pass
questions: Which module calls `owner_sessions.end_expired_sessions` every 60 seconds, as the changed State 3 passage now requires?

quotes:
The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: State 3 assigns the running instance and its 60-second owner_sessions pass to module:instance_lifecycle.

topics.topic: Required failure handling for the periodic session-expiration pass
questions: What must `module:instance_lifecycle` and the running instance do if the periodic expiration pass or one of its lock/session operations fails?

quotes:
`module:owner_sessions`. The pass, every 60 seconds from the start, that
ends every session that has reached a limit (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: The State 5 public operation contract declares that owner_sessions.end_expired_sessions has no error outcome, so lifecycle needs no failure-handling branch for this operation.
